source_review.notes: Checked primary GFS, Azure LRC, f4, and Tiger research plus current official HDFS, Ceph, CRUSH, and Colossus material. Sources support full replication, k+m erasure coding, systematic/MDS reconstruction, topology-aware placement, degraded operation, recovery, repair locality, mutable/cold-tier trade-offs, and redundancy adaptation. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed k data, m parity, n total fragments, fragment size c, stripe payload, amplification, efficiency, valid fragment sets, erasure margin, replication factor, and repair variables.
Checked MDS terminology is explicitly distinguished from metadata server and that count claims remain conditional on compatible valid fragment indices and placement.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical bytes, encoded fragments, copies, failure domains, integrity state, and probabilistic events remain separate.

evidence: Executed protection-capacity-repair with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 640-MiB stripe payload, 896-MiB encoded stripe, factor 1.40, 160 stripes, capacity totals, and repair totals.
Recomputed 100 GiB as 160 full 640-MiB stripes, triple replication as 322,122,547,200 bytes, coding as 150,323,855,360 bytes, and the difference as 171,798,691,840 bytes.
Recomputed exercises as 72, 33, and 32 TiB for triple, 8+3, and 12+4 protection and as 640-MiB read versus 64-MiB write for one modeled coded repair.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All capacity comparisons are labeled ideal full-stripe payload and omit operational overhead.

evidence: Derived coded amplification as (k+m)/k and efficiency as k/(k+m) from equal-sized full-stripe fragments.
Checked replication erasure tolerance r-1 and MDS stripe decodability from at least k compatible valid fragments.
Reviewed the independent identical no-repair binomial tail and p^r formulas with every assumption and non-forecast limitation stated.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Deterministic tolerance does not become a time-based durability probability without a justified stochastic model.

evidence: Reviewed full/partial stripes, tiny objects, immutable and mutable data, partial overwrite, degraded acknowledgement/read, exactly-k margin, fewer-than-k loss, corrupt versus missing fragments, and incompatible code profiles.

Reviewed shared host/rack/power/network/firmware/operator/key domains, stale topology, full destinations, repair storms, overloaded survivors, mixed-version upgrades, migration crash/retry, and old-policy cleanup.
Reviewed metadata/key loss, sensitive fragments, tenant leakage, snapshots/holds, deletion across parity and temporary data, and archival/research governance.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Single-fragment erasures are not used as a substitute for correlated-fault, silent-corruption, or recovery-path testing.

evidence: Traced object/version/profile identity, fragment index/length/checksum, current valid sets, domain placement, acknowledgement, commit, repair source verification, and policy migration through exposition and examples.
Checked that decodable, available, protected, durable, consistent, and intact states are never treated as synonyms.
Checked old protection is retained until new fragments decode to the authoritative logical digest and cutover is committed.
invariant_checking.notes: Configured policy and physical fragment presence alone do not prove current recoverability.

evidence: Reviewed all ten protection-policy audit obligations from unit/version and code profile through topology, repair, migration, and restore testing.

Checked counterexamples for copies-equal-domains, parity-equals-checksum, readable-equals-protected, ideal-ratio-equals-installed-capacity, failure-independence, configured-equals-acknowledged, healthy-device-equals-healthy-fragment, and toggle-equals-migration claims.
Reviewed deterministic reconstruction, topology placement, verified-input repair, partial-write commit, migration cutover, and probabilistic-model boundaries.
proof_review.notes: Coding theory, systems correctness, empirical durability, performance, security, and governance require distinct evidence.

evidence: Audited uses of tolerate, any, recover, valid, verified, independent, exact, safe, durable, protected, and proof.
Confirmed fixture and formulas are labeled full-stripe conditional models rather than coding implementations, installed-capacity forecasts, or production durability estimates.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Implementation-specific recovery patterns and advanced repair optimizations are not generalized beyond cited scope.

evidence: Reviewed retrieval dates, workload/object-size distributions, topology inventories, integrity/scrub age, acknowledgement sets, failure histories, repair duration, degraded latency, migration trials, and restores.
Confirmed no universal code optimum, capacity saving, durability nines, performance result, ethical approval, certification, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production claims require exact code/library/profile, topology, workloads, fault processes, repair controls, key/metadata recovery, and repeated observed evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed replication, systematic k+m coding, finite-field intuition, failure domains, probability limits, integrity, writes, degraded reads, repair, local reconstruction, scrubbing, migration, capacity, security, and evidence as one protection model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed profile metadata, placement rules, degraded I/O, partial writes, idempotent repair, throttling, topology audits, capacity reserve, upgrade compatibility, policy migration, telemetry, fault injection, and restore drills. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from recovery information and code math through topology, protocols, repair, lifecycle, and governance; ten examples and five complete answers cover capacity, domain correlation, partial writes, repair amplification, and archival transition.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external coding theorist, storage researcher, filesystem operator, storage vendor, security auditor, research-ethics authority, archive custodian, or certification review is claimed.
